pending.h: Spencer Brown Says Fury Fight Is On Despite Health Claims
pending.sum: Spencer Brown says there is no diagnosis behind the schizophrenia reports, that Fury is in great spirits, and that the Joshua fight is happening.
pending.q: there's no way in the world that Tyson Fury was schizophrenic
body: Spencer Brown shot down recent reports about Tyson Fury's mental health. He said there is no diagnosis, that the issue is historical, and that it resurfaced because of a comment in a documentary segment that he says was never due to air.

Brown called the coverage sensationalism and said Fury has been open about his mental health struggles and should be praised for it, not criticised. He said the boxing board has cleared Fury to fight and that there was never any doubt about it.

He also said Anthony Joshua's side got in touch to ask if Fury was all right and if the fight was still on. Brown's answer: “The fight's on.” He said he speaks to Fury every day, that Fury is in the best headspace he has seen him in, and that he arrives in England next week.
Why it matters: With the fight two weeks away, the headlines had raised questions about whether it would go ahead. Brown's camp is now saying it will, and that Fury is fit to fight.

pending.h: Napper Says Eubank Jr vs Brook Decision Due In Days
pending.sum: Eubank Jr's manager says a decision on a Kell Brook fight is coming within days. He also gave the likely weight, location and timing.
pending.q: It's closer than it's ever been ever before.
pending.who: Napper, manager of Chris Eubank Jr
pending.ctx: Interview with Boxing King Media in Dubai
body: Napper says talks for Chris Eubank Jr vs Kell Brook are further along than at any earlier point. He says the camp is “more hot than cold”. A decision on whether the fight happens should come in the next couple of days, though he wouldn't say when an announcement might follow.

He says the team is trying to get a few things over the line. If they do, there's a fight. If they don't, there isn't. He wouldn't say who would promote it, noting that Eubank Jr is a free agent who can work with whoever offers the most.

On the details, Napper says it would be at super middleweight with no weight clauses on either fighter. The location would probably be the UK, and the timing is “First quarter of next year.” He says Eubank Jr has long been up for the fight and has wanted it since Brook beat Khan.

Why it matters: A Eubank Jr vs Brook fight would be a big domestic night in the UK, and Napper says any other names linked to Eubank Jr, including Conor Benn, are off the table until this one is settled.

pending.h: Kape Tells Van His Title Reign Ends In Toronto
pending.sum: Manel Kape says he's on another level from champion Joshua Van and predicts a body-head attack that ends with Van dropped in Toronto.
pending.q: You cannot compare me and him. This is this is a big insult.
body: Manel Kape says flyweight champion Joshua Van's time is up. Speaking to MMA Fighting before their UFC 336 fight in Toronto, Kape said he has no hard feelings and isn't underestimating Van. But he called this "the end of the road" and said the belt is going home with him.

Kape said he was more impressed by how Pantoja fought than by Van's performance. He said Pantoja was emotional in that fight and paid the price. He gave Van credit for maturity on the ground, but he dismissed his striking as that of a regular fighter and said they are in different levels.

He was blunt about the gap. Kape said “whatever Joshua Van do, I do I do 10 times better.” As for how it ends, he predicts a body-head attack that wears Van down, followed by a finish. In his words, he'll “drop him like I drop everyone.”
Why it matters: Kape has waited a long time for this title shot and is selling it as a changing of the guard. His confidence adds some edge to a flyweight title fight that is usually respectful.
